title: 火锅分几派③北京铜锅涮羊肉：一锅清水，凭什么封神 | China Hotpot Schools P3 · Beijing 🐑
description:
清水锅底 vs 麻辣红汤，你站哪一派？评论区聊聊。

【火锅分几派·第3集 北京铜锅涮羊肉】别的火锅比锅底，北京铜锅偏偏用清水——不放辣、不放油，只丢几段葱、几片姜、一把海米枸杞。凭什么封神？靠的是一口中间带烟囱的紫铜炭火锅，炭火把汤顶得永远微滚，薄羊肉片「七上八下」几秒就熟。真正的灵魂在蘸料：二八麻酱（二分花生、八分芝麻澥开），再加韭菜花、酱豆腐、卤虾油。这一锅涮了一百多年，1903 年东来顺就是从东安市场一个小摊起家的。清水见真章，北京话叫一声——敞亮！

While other hotpots compete on broth, Beijing's copper pot uses plain water — no chili, no oil, just scallion, ginger and a few dried shrimp. Its magic is the chimneyed copper charcoal pot that keeps the water at a gentle boil, cooking paper-thin mutton in seconds. The real soul is the dip: sesame paste cut with peanut (the '2-and-8' blend), plus chive flower, fermented tofu and shrimp oil. This pot has simmered for a century — Donglaishun began in 1903 as a market stall. Plain water, real skill.

AI-assisted edit; the bilingual subtitles are the narration — no voiceover. Facts checked this run; sources below. Food culture, not dietary advice. Footage licensed from Pexels (credited below).
